items.fca-ai-guidance::consumer-duty: Firms must be able to demonstrate that AI use delivers good consumer outcomes under the Consumer Duty, including monitoring for disparate impacts and providing appropriate redress where AI causes harm.
items.fca-ai-guidance::testing-validation: Firms should establish proportionate testing and validation regimes for AI before and during deployment, accounting for data quality, model performance, drift and the firm's wider control environment.
items.fca-ai-guidance::governance-accountabili: Firms remain fully accountable for AI outcomes; there should be a dedicated individual responsible for the AI system's role in regulated business activities and for its effective control.
items.fca-ai-guidance::operational-resilience: Firms must ensure AI supports the delivery of their important business services within established impact tolerances, including contingency plans, incident management, and recovery procedures for disruption involving AI systems.
items.fca-ai-guidance::third-party-risk: Firms must manage third-party risk associated with AI systems throughout the life span of the arrangement, including vendor due diligence, contractual requirements, and monitoring of third-party AI providers, with greater risk management as dependence on outsourced providers increases.
